newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling to get loans from Bank of China.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling to get loans from Bank of China.

text.p: Jiangling Motors Corp Ltd will receive US$90 million and 50 million yuan in loans from the Bank of China (BOC), the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Friday.
An agreement on the loans were signed between Jiangling and the BOC on Thursday in Nanchang, capital of Jiangxi province, the newspaper said.
Jiangling plans to use the loans, which will be offered by the end of this year, to supplement its working capital, the newspaper said, without giving other details.

The loans followed another in September this year when the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) agreed to extend Jiangling a 200 million-yuan loan to add to the firm's working capital, the newspaper said.
Part of the 200 million yuan will be disbursed by end-1996, with the remainder early next year, it said.

A company spokesman in September told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that Jiangling would receive 70 million yuan from the ICBC by the end of this year, with the remaining 130 million yuan to be disbursed in the first quarter of 1997.
He declined to provide details of the interest rate or maturity of the loan.
The official said Jiangling planned to channel the 200 million yuan mainly into production of automobile engines.
The Securities Times earlier said Jiangling planned to use up to US$1.3 billion in foreign exchange over the next five years to expand its core operations.
The newspaper said Jiangling had set up a unit in Nanchang to conduct foreign exchange financing business in a bid to raise substantial amounts of funds at low cost.
Jiangling also plans to take advantage of the U.S. automobile titan Ford Motor Co's global influence to raise funds needed for expansion and technological upgrading, it said.
Ford last year paid about US$40 million to purchase 80 percent of Jiangling's issue of 174 million class B shares.
